messages.subject: Improving performance of map reduce job
parts:
Problem:
I have two files each of size approx. 230 MB.The file format is like
this

Each record has four fields seperated by space.
The second field in each file is unique. For example;
xx sss 21 256.(here sss in one file is unique but it can appear in
another file)

First field represents project name
second field ..pagename
third field ---page views and the forth field page size.

Now given a project name we need to get the top 10 page name in the
decreasing order of their page views.
That means if a page name is appearing in more than file than we need
to add their page views.

So my first map reduce job is to read the first field and emit the
page name as key and the page view as value and in the reduction part
i will add the page views.

4 library(Rhipe)
5 rhinit()
6 map<-expression({
7 y<-do.call("rbind",lapply(map.values,function(r){
8 strsplit(r," ")[[1]]
9 }))
10
11
12
14 if(nrow(y > 0))
15 {
16 for( i in 1:nrow(y))
17 {
18 x<-y[i, ]
19 if(x[1] == "en")
20 {
21 key<-x[2]
22 value<-as.numeric(x[3])
23 rhcollect(key,value)
24 }
25
26 }
27 }
28
29
30 })
31
32 reduce<-expression(
33 pre = { sums=0 } ,
34 reduce = {
35 sums <- sum(sums,unlist(reduce.values))
36 },
37 post = {
38 rhcollect(reduce.key,sums)
39 }
40
41 )
42
43
44 mapred<-list(rhipe_map_buff_size=20,mapred.task.timeout=0)
45 ifolder="wikistat_sample" #consist of single file
46 ofolder="/out_multi"
48 z<-
rhmr(map=map,reduce=reduce,inout=c("text","sequence"),ifolder=ifolder,
ofolder=ofolder,mapred=mapred,job name="DataMining_MultiFile")
49 rhex(z)


In the second map reduce job i am creating a data frame and then
ordering them according to their page views
1 library(Rhipe)
2 rhinit()
3 map<-expression({
4
5 y<-do.call("rbind",lapply(seq_along(map.values),function(i) x<-
c(map.keys[[i]],map.values[[i]])))
6
7
8 page.name = y[,1]

11 d<-
data.frame(page.name=page.name,page.views=page.views,stringsAsFactors=FALSE)

15

17

rbind(collect,do.call("rbind",reduce.values))

$page.views),decreasing=TRUE), ]
23 },
24 post = {
25
26 collect<-collect[1:min(nrow(collect),10),]
27 rhcollect(reduce.key,collect)
28 }
29
30 )
31

33 ifolder = "/out_multi"
34 ofolder = "/out3_multi"
35
36 z<-rhmr(map = map,reduce =
reduce,inout=c("sequence","sequence"),ifolder = ifolder,ofolder =
ofolder,mapred=mapred,jobnam e="DataSort1")
37 rhex(z)
38


The first map reduce job took 11 min and the second map reduce job
took more than 1 hour to complete.

I tried setting the parameter combiner=TRUE in the firstmap reduce job
to do the reduction locally but no luck.
Well i think the creation of the data frame in the second map reduce
job is the bottle neck but i dont have other way to solve this
problem.
i am evaluating another approach without creating the data frame in
the second map reduce job.\

Can you please have a look on the code above and suggest me some
pointers to improve the efficiency?

Regards,
Shekhar

In the second map, why don't you only send the top ten entries instead all of d?

13 d<-d[order(as.numeric(d$page.views),decreasing=TRUE), ]
d = d[ 1: min(nrow(d),10),,drop=FALSE]
14 rhcollect("en",d)

Also in the second, have you considered using combiner=TRUE ?

messages.author: 5b0c9158bfa781ba
messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Re: Improving performance of map reduce job
parts:
Time your code

1. The tedious approach is a) empty map / no reduce : time taken to go
over the data and send to R b) map contains lapply+strsplit and
nothing else - time taken to go over the data and tokenize c) and so
on.

2. Use system.time to compute different times of different segments of
the code and output via rhcollect or via rhcounter (remember to
convert fractional times to integers)
